title: Hide-and-seek: Threshold values and contribution towards better understanding of recovery rate in microplastic research
author: Dimante-Deimantovica, Suhareva, et al.

steps.title: Prepare spiked water sample
steps.instruction: Add 100 polystyrene (PS) beads (Ø 100 µm) to 100 mL of filtered Milli‑Q water in a clean beaker; this will be the starting sample for all experiments.

steps.title: Vacuum‑filtration extraction (method a)
steps.instruction: Perform nine successive filtration cycles using a borosilicate vacuum‑filtration assembly (top funnel, filter holder, filtering flask) equipped with a stainless‑steel 10 µm mesh filter (Ø 47 mm) fixed with an aluminium clamp (VWR). After each cycle rinse the beaker and top funnel thoroughly, save the filter in a Petri dish, rinse the top funnel and filter its contents on a second 10 µm filter placed in a clean filtration apparatus, examine both filters under a microscope, then flush the retained beads from the filters into a clean beaker. Repeat the whole cycle eight more times (total 9 cycles). After the final cycle check the rinsed filters and Petri dish under a binocular to confirm no beads remain.

substeps.instruction: Place 10 µm stainless‑steel filter (Ø 47 mm) in the filtration apparatus.
Pour the spiked sample onto the filter; rinse the beaker and top funnel multiple times to recover beads.
Collect the filter in a Petri dish.
Rinse the top funnel, filter its rinse through a second 10 µm filter in a clean apparatus.
Inspect both filters under a microscope and record bead numbers.
Flush beads from each filter into a clean beaker.
Repeat steps a–f eight additional times.
After the ninth cycle, examine all rinsed filters and the Petri dish with a binocular to ensure no beads remain.

steps.title: Sieve extraction (method b)
steps.instruction: Perform nine successive sieving cycles using a woven‑wire stainless‑steel sieve (50 µm mesh, Ø 100 mm, RETSCH). After each sieving, rinse the beaker thoroughly, collect beads rinsed from the sieve in a clean beaker, count beads under a binocular, then repeat the process eight more times (total 9 cycles).

substeps.instruction: Place the 50 µm stainless‑steel sieve (Ø 100 mm) in a clean setup.
Pour the spiked sample onto the sieve; rinse the beaker multiple times to recover beads.
Rinse beads retained on the sieve into a clean beaker.
Count beads under a binocular.
Repeat steps a–d eight additional times.

steps.title: Freshwater sediment protocol no.1
steps.instruction: Process each 100 mL spiked sample through eight consecutive purification steps followed by a final preservative step, as detailed below. After each treatment step filter the suspension through a 10 µm filter (vacuum assembly), flush beads into the next step, and rinse all beakers and top funnels multiple times.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 mL of 30 % H₂O₂ to the sample.
Incubate in a shaking water bath for 24 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Flush beads with filtered Milli‑Q water into a clean beaker, freeze at –20 °C, then place in a vacuum freeze‑dryer for 48 h.
Filter the dried sample through a 10 µm filter; flush beads into a separatory funnel containing heavy liquid (density 1.75 kg L⁻¹) up to two‑thirds of the funnel volume.
Manually shake the funnel for 5 min to aerate, then let stand for 24 h to settle.
Drain the settled (bottom) phase, keep it for the next separation; pour the top phase onto a fresh 10 µm filter, rinse the funnel interior with filtered Milli‑Q water, and collect the filtrate.
Return the settled phase to the funnel, aerate 5 min, settle 24 h; repeat the density‑separation cycle three times total.
After each density separation, flush beads from the 10 µm filter with up to 200 mL of 5 % SDS solution (total volume ≤200 mL) into a beaker; incubate 48 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Flush beads with 300 mL of TRIS buffer (pH 8.2) into a beaker, add 0.5 mL alcalase, incubate 48 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Flush beads with 300 mL of acetate buffer (pH 4.8) into a beaker, add 0.5 mL viscozyme and 0.5 mL cellulase, incubate 48 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.

Flush beads with 200 mL filtered Milli‑Q water into a 1 L beaker, cool to 15–20 °C, then add 145 mL 50 % H₂O₂, 65 mL 0.1 M NaOH, and 62 mL 0.1 M FeSO₄; keep at 20–30 °C for ≥4 h, then stand overnight.
Filter the mixture, flush beads into a separatory funnel with heavy liquid (density 1.75 kg L⁻¹) and repeat the density‑separation cycle as described above (second separation).
Wash beads with filtered Milli‑Q water followed by 50 % ethanol; flush into a clean beaker containing 50 % ethanol and store at 40 °C for two weeks.
All beakers, top funnels and filter housings are rinsed thoroughly multiple times after each transfer.

steps.title: Freshwater sediment protocol no.2 (modified)
steps.instruction: Follow protocol no.1 with the following modifications: swap the pre‑oxidation and freezing steps; perform each density‑separation (first and second) twice instead of three times; during the TRIS‑buffer enzymatic step add 0.5 mL alcalase **and** 0.5 mL protease; omit the final ethanol preservation step. Conduct three replicates.

substeps.instruction: Step 1: Freeze the sample (‑20 °C) and freeze‑dry 48 h.
Step 2: Add 50 mL 30 % H₂O₂, incubate 24 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Step 3: Perform density‑separation 1 twice (as in protocol no.1).
Step 4: SDS treatment as in protocol no.1.
Step 5: TRIS‑buffer enzymatic treatment – add 0.5 mL alcalase **and** 0.5 mL protease; incubate 48 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Step 6: Acetate‑buffer enzymatic treatment as in protocol no.1.
Step 7: Fenton reaction as in protocol no.1.
Step 8: Density‑separation 2 twice (as in protocol no.1).
No ethanol preservation step.
Rinse all equipment thoroughly after each transfer.

steps.title: Marine sediment protocol
steps.instruction: Apply five consecutive purification steps to each sample, using the same filtration and rinsing routine as above.

substeps.instruction: Density‑separation 1 performed twice (two separations).
Pre‑oxidation: add 30 % H₂O₂ (volume as in protocol no.1) and incubate 24 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Enzymatic treatment in TRIS buffer: add 0.5 mL protease only, incubate 48 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Enzymatic treatment in acetate buffer: add 0.5 mL viscozyme, 0.5 mL cellulase, and 0.1 mL chitinase; incubate 48 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Density‑separation 2 performed once (single separation).
After each step filter through a 10 µm filter, flush beads forward, and rinse all vessels multiple times.

steps.title: Marine surface water protocol
steps.instruction: Process each sample through three chemical treatment steps, filtering and rinsing between steps.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 mL of 10 % NaOH to the sample; incubate 24 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm in a shaking water bath.
Filter, then flush beads with 100 mL filtered Milli‑Q water into a clean beaker; add 200 mL of 30 % H₂O₂; incubate 24 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
Add 300 mL acetate buffer (pH 4.8) together with 0.5 mL viscozyme and 0.5 mL cellulase; incubate 48 h at +50 °C, 100 rpm.
After each treatment filter through a 10 µm filter, flush beads into the next step, and rinse all equipment thoroughly.

steps.title: Density‑separation volume experiment
steps.instruction: Compare recoverability using separatory funnels of 250 mL, 500 mL and 1000 mL while keeping the sample size constant (100 mL spiked water with 100 PS beads mixed with wet sediment). Perform three consecutive density‑separation cycles with heavy liquid (density 1.75 kg L⁻¹) in each funnel size as described in the density‑separation steps of protocol no.1, recording bead recovery after each cycle.

substeps.instruction: Prepare three identical samples (100 mL, 100 PS beads, wet sediment).
Place each sample in a separatory funnel of the designated volume (250 mL, 500 mL, 1000 mL).
Add heavy liquid up to two‑thirds of the funnel volume, aerate manually for 5 min, let settle 24 h.
Collect the top phase, filter through a 10 µm filter, rinse funnel interior with filtered Milli‑Q water, and flush beads into a clean beaker.
Return the settled phase to the funnel, repeat aeration and settling for a total of three separations.
Count beads after each separation to calculate total and step‑wise recoverability for each funnel size.
